title: A writer who defines ambiguous terms before they appear takes from the reader the choice of which meaning each one carries
body:
- Defining a term before it is used takes the choice of meaning out of the reader's hands, because an unconstrained reader will pick from the surface reading rather than the one the writer needed.
- Pairing the definition with one or two example usages anchors the chosen sense and prevents the reader from sliding back into an alternative reading.
- A systematic review of communication failures identified disambiguation as one of six recurring themes.
- Case: In a word sense disambiguation test on a large language model, supplying definitions plus examples raised accuracy to 82.3%; removing definitions dropped accuracy by 12-15 percentage points.
conversion: The reader's freedom to choose among plausible meanings becomes a meaning the writer selected in advance.
